parts:
Annie, thanks for the question.

The compilation error is coming from the specification of the returnType() statement in your definition of the S_i function.  In the definition of S_i, you declare the return type to be a *vector*:
    returnType(double(1))
But in reality this function returns a scalar, and you should change the returnType specification to:
    returnType(double(0))
I think that will solve the compilation problem.

Regarding the -Inf and NaN values you're seeing, these come from some numerical issues in your model.  You can diagnose these a little bit using code such as:

> model$logProb_x
 [1] -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf  NaN  NaN
[16]  NaN  NaN  NaN  Inf  Inf  Inf  NaN  NaN  NaN  NaN

The NaN's are resulting from the calculation inside the S_i function, where when the argument i > 13, for example: 

> S_i(14)
[1] 0

gives zero (this comes from pgamma(x, k, rate = r), where x represents the value of i, and this calculation rounds to 1).  When S_i(i) returns the value 0, this gives a division by 0 in the dpois_t() function, and hence NaN.

I think you can fix these numerical issues in S_i by making all these probability calculations take place on the log scale.  This would involve using arguments such as:

pgamma(... log.p = TRUE, lower.tail = FALSE)

inside the S_i function, then also doing calculations inside the dpois_t function on the log scale.

Similarly, for the -Inf values, those are coming about from the calculation of dpois(x, mu) (in the dpois_t function) rounding to 0, and hence prob=0, and log(prob) is -Inf.  Once again, if you do all these calculations on the log scale, it should fix this problem.  For the return statements in dpois_t, I would change that (after calculating the value of logprob, all calculations on the log scale) to:

    if(log) return(logprob))
    else return(exp(logprob))

Let me know if this all makes sense, and keep at it.  I hope you can get your model working.

Also, I was happy to see your use of the basicMCMCplots package.

Cheers,
Daniel
On Wed, Dec 20, 2023 at 3:13 PM Annie Shapiro <ashap...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hello, 

I am hoping to code a truncated likelihood. In the users manual, you state  x ~ dnorm(0, sd = 10) T(0, a) gives the normal probability density divided by its intergral from 0 to a. However, I am interested in coding a truncated distribution where the denominator is the integral of a different density. To do this, I created my own truncated Poisson distribution, but I am getting -Inf and NaN for the log probability of one of my variables and the following error when I try to compile my model:

Error: Number of dimensions 1 of the return() argument does not match number 0 given in the returnType() statement. This occurred for: return(log(prob)) This was part of the call: { return(log(prob)) }

Below is my code and attached is the data I'm using. Any help in troubleshooting would be much appreciated!

Best,
Annie

library(nimble)
library(dplyr)
library(readxl)
library(ggplot2)
library(basicMCMCplots)
set.seed(1)

dat <- read_excel("ex_dat.xlsx") 

k <- 8.07
r <- 4.12
x0 <- 2012


#2007
p0 <- 1-(1-1/2.3)^(k/r)

#2017
p1 <- 1-(1-1/2.6)^(k/r)

#make bottom 0 because that is what the equation likes
l <- p1-p0

#slope
# s <- (p1-p0)/(2016-2007)

dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(p = l/(1+exp(.5*(Year-x0)))+ p0)

#====================================================================
# functions
#====================================================================

f_vec <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0),
                 p = double(0)){
   
    k <- 8.07
    r <- 4.12

    tmp_vec <- rep(NA, x)
   
    for (i in 1:x) {
      tmp_vec[i] <- p*(pgamma(x-(i-1), k, rate = r) - pgamma(x-i, k, rate = r))
    }
   
    return(tmp_vec)
    returnType(double(1))
  })

# truncation function
S_i <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0)){
   
    k <- 8.07
    r <- 4.12
   
    out <- 1-pgamma(x, k, rate = r)
   
    return(out)
    returnType(double(1))
  })

# code penalty as prior
dpen <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1),
                 theta = double(0), L = double(0),
                 log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    logProb <- -(theta/2)*sum((log(x[1:(L-2)]) - 2*log(x[2:(L-1)]) + log(x[3:L]))^2)
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
  })


# code truncated likelihood
dpois_t <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(0),
                mu = double(0), i = double(0),
                log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
   
    prob <- dpois(x, mu)/S_i(i)
    # logProb <- log(prob)
   
    if(log) return(log(prob))
    else return(prob)
  })

#====================================================================
# set up MCMC
#====================================================================
modelCode <- nimbleCode({
 
  for (i in 1:L){
    #get mu
    mu[i] <- sum(f_vec(i, p[i])*lambda[1:i])
   
    #likelihood -- this is what I'd like to truncate
    x[i] ~ dpois_t(mu = mu[i], i=i)
    }
 
  #priors
  lambda[1:L] ~ dpen(theta = theta, L = L)
})



modelConsts <- list(L = nrow(dat),
                    # I = 1:nrow(dat),
                    p = dat$p,  
                    theta = 1000)

modelData <- list(x = dat$Notifications)

initsList <- list(lambda = abs(rnorm(nrow(dat), mean(dat$Notifications), sd(dat$Notifications))))

model <- nimbleModel(modelCode, data = modelData,  inits = initsList, constants = modelConsts)
model$initializeInfo()
model$calculate()

model$x
model$lambda
model$mu

model$logProb_lambda
model$logProb_x

#====================================================================
# Compile and run model
#====================================================================

# compile into nimble
Cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
